item.title: Two more arrested over viral Nadi robbery
item.description: Two more suspects allegedly involved in the aggravated robbery of a taxi driver in Nadi yesterday morning, are now in Police custody. Police say the development follows the surrender of the first suspect yesterday, after a video of the alleged robbery went viral.
item.content:encoded:
Two more suspects allegedly involved in the aggravated robbery of a taxi driver in Nadi yesterday morning, are now in Police custody.

Police say the development follows the surrender of the first suspect yesterday, after a video of the alleged robbery went viral.

The Western Division Taskforce is continuing its search for a fourth suspect, whose identity is known to Police.

Investigations into the incident continue.

item.title: More than 300 student cases reported to Substance Abuse Advisory Council this year - Naisele
item.description: More than 300 cases involving students have been reported to the Substance Abuse Advisory Council so far this year, mostly involving bullying, disrespectful behaviour and other behavioural issues. Speaking to about 2,000 women during the Methodist Women’s Conference at the World Harvest Centre, Director of the Substance Abuse Advisory Council Josua Naisele says students are facing growing social c
item.content:encoded:
More than 300 cases involving students have been reported to the Substance Abuse Advisory Council so far this year, mostly involving bullying, disrespectful behaviour and other behavioural issues.

Speaking to about 2,000 women during the Methodist Women’s Conference at the World Harvest Centre, Director of the Substance Abuse Advisory Council Josua Naisele says students are facing growing social challenges , including bullying, peer pressure, social media, violence and, in some cases, drug use.

He is urging parents to better understand what their children are going through before judging them.

Naisele says there have also been a few cases they received involved drugs and cyberbullying.

He says many behavioural issues among students can be linked to peer pressure, curiosity, social media and the environments in which children grow up.

Naisele says peer pressure remains a major challenge, as some children may be influenced by friends who introduce them to behaviour that are not encouraged at home .

He says some students may also turn to drugs as a way of coping with problems, while curiosity can lead young people to experiment with smoking and other harmful behaviour.

Naisele says children can also be influenced by what they see around them, including violence and drug use in their homes and communities.

He says social media and access to the internet have added another challenge, with young people being exposed to content that may not be suitable for them.

Naisele is urging parents to build stronger connections with their children through communication, understanding and positive support.

He says simply living under the same roof does not necessarily mean parents and children are connected .

Naisele says parents should create a home environment where children feel respected and supported and are comfortable enough to talk about the problems they are facing.

He is also urging parents not to immediately judge their children when they open up about their problems, as this can affect them emotionally and make it more difficult for them to seek help.

Naisele says students should not be afraid to seek counselling, stressing that counselling is about supporting them rather than judging them.

He says counsellors listen to students and guide them towards the support they need, while cases involving drugs, cyberbullying and other serious matters are referred to the relevant authorities.

Naisele says the Methodist Women’s Conference is an important platform, as the women will return to their churches, villages and communities across Fiji and Rotuma with the knowledge shared during the conference.

He says the women were encouraged to first apply what they have learned in their own lives and families before sharing the message with others.

Naisele says stronger communication, awareness and understanding within families can help provide students with the support they need to deal with the challenges they face in their daily lives.

item.title: Country music legend Dolly Parton dies aged 80
item.description: Country music legend Dolly Parton, one of the world’s most celebrated singer-songwriters and philanthropists, has died aged 80. Her death was announced by her nephew, Brian Seaver, on Instagram.
item.content:encoded:
Country music legend Dolly Parton, one of the world’s most celebrated singer-songwriters and philanthropists, has died aged 80.

Her death was announced by her nephew, Brian Seaver, on Instagram.

Parton was known for her powerful songwriting, distinctive voice and colourful personality.

She wrote some of country music’s most famous songs, including Jolene and I Will Always Love You .

She scored 25 US country number-one singles and had 47 albums reach the country Top 10. Her 1980 hit 9 to 5 also topped the US pop charts and earned her an Oscar nomination.

Parton was also a successful actress, appearing in films including 9 to 5 , The Best Little Whorehouse in Texas and Steel Magnolias .

Born into poverty in Tennessee, Parton grew up in a family of 12 children.

She began singing in church and performed at the Grand Ole Opry at the age of 13.

She moved to Nashville after finishing high school in 1964 and began her career as a songwriter before becoming a recording artist.

Her partnership with Porter Wagoner helped launch her career, while her later duet with Kenny Rogers, Islands in the Stream , became another major hit.

Parton was also widely praised for her philanthropy. Her Imagination Library literacy programme has provided more than 150 million books to children.

She was married to Carl Dean from 1966 until her death, with the couple renewing their vows in 2016 to mark their 50th wedding anniversary.

Parton won 10 Grammy Awards and remained one of country music’s most recognisable and beloved figures for decades. S ource: The Guardian

item.title: RFMF armoury break-in accused Ledua late to court due to traffic
item.description: Ledua appeared before Justice Tuiqereqere after a bench warrant was issued this morning when he failed to appear in court. The bench warrant was later cancelled after Ledua appeared and explained the reason for his delay.
item.content:encoded:
Ledua appeared before Justice Tuiqereqere after a bench warrant was issued this morning when he failed to appear in court.

The bench warrant was later cancelled after Ledua appeared and explained the reason for his delay.

Justice Tuiqereqere told Ledua that traffic is an everyday problem and warned him that he would face consequences for failing to attend court.

Meanwhile, hi s lawyer, Jerry Dinati informed the court that he intends to challenge the DNA report, which, he said was obtained without Ledua's knowledge.

Ledua is charged with one count of aggravated burglary and one count of damaging property.

It is alleged that between April 8th and 9th, Ledua attempted to break into the RFMF Ammunition Magazine building in Nabua and damaged the door lock keypad.

The matter has been adjourned to September 10th.
